reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: 1× updateEntityColumn on one root, then channel.flush(); one effect on the root runs once
reading.floor: 1× root(v) with no batch; the alien effect on the root runs after every write
reading.caveat: ONE OPERATION IS 1 WRITES TO ONE ROOT AND ONE SETTLE, with one effect reading the root. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: frame coalescing against per-write delivery. Ours enlists the effect on the first write of the frame, finds it already changed in this frame on every later write, and runs the body once at the flush. Alien-signals with no batch runs the effect synchronously at the end of every write, so the body runs 1 times per operation. EXPECTED DIRECTION [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]: with a single write ours pays the flush and alien pays nothing extra, so ours is above alien there; as writes per frame grow, alien pays one effect run per write and ours pays one in total, so the ratio is expected to fall. The batched row at the largest count is the fairness check. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
